- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or low (especially <0.15) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust for recent sentiment shifts to reduce lag.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model overcorrects downward — reduce forecast slope for 2–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high for 3–7 days after peak sentiment; apply downward pressure if sentiment drops below 0.15.
- For 30-day forecasts, model overestimates early days (1–5) when sentiment is rising, then underestimates late days (25–30) when sentiment is falling — apply smoothing to mid-to-late horizon.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.09–0.18), reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid “sentiment-blind” overconfidence.
